name: יוֹכֶבֶד
summary: A daughter of Levi, born to him in Egypt, the wife of Amram and mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam (Exo 6:20; Num 26:59); the unnamed “daughter of Levi” who hid Moses three months and nursed him for Pharaoh's daughter (Exo 2:1–9), by faith, as Hebrews says (Heb 11:23). The name is יוֹ, the short form of Yahweh's name that begins names such as יוֹנָתָן, with כֶבֶד from the root of כָּבוֹד: “Yah is glory”, or “Yah is weighty, honoured”. Phoenician names are formed the same way with kbd, “glory”, as an epithet of a god (kbdmlqrt, “Milqart is the glory”). Scripture gives no explanation of the name.

evidence.note: “Amram took יוֹכֶבֶד his father's sister as wife, and she bore him Aaron and Moses.”
“The name of Amram's wife was יוֹכֶבֶד, daughter of Levi, whom she bore to Levi in Egypt; and she bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister.”
“A daughter of Levi” bore a son and hid him three months.
She nursed the child for Pharaoh's daughter.
“By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden three months by his parents … and they were not afraid of the king's command.”
The glory (כָּבוֹד) of Yahweh that her son asked to see.
Phoenician kbd “glory, epithet of divinity”, in names: kbdmlqrt “Milqart is the Glory”.

note: BDB files the name under יהו (e.az.bo), as a name of Yahweh; it is linked here because its second element is the root כבד. The form כֶבֶד (segolate) is not the adjective; it is read as a noun “glory, weight” like כֹּבֶד. Exo 6:20 calls her דֹּדָתוֹ, Amram's aunt.
